geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass from a simple lift into a split-wing form to create an explicit public seam/court toward the street frontage while keeping the mass continuous in ancestry.
Choose the long-axis split so the new void becomes a readable lateral ground response rather than a random cut.
Open a meaningful gap to strengthen void publicness and make the access edge legible.
Preserve a grounded connector so the composition remains one massing idea with a clear anchor instead of two disconnected fragments.
Keep the opening as a true void rather than closing it with a bridge, so the public threshold is unmistakable.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the blunt lifted block logic with a split-wing strategy so the mass can open a legible public threshold toward the access edge while preserving one dominant body.
Reduce the lift so the ground plane remains more continuous and the building does not read as an overly sealed floating box.
Strengthen the support-to-body relation to make the base legible and improve the perceived program anchor at ground.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent low bar with a slightly lifted/skewed end, so the dominant gesture and hierarchy are reasonably clear. However, for neighborhood living the visible mass under-serves the required public threshold: the blue frontage edge is met by a mostly sealed body with only a small undercut, and the open-space figure is not legible as a meaningful court/terrace. The silhouette is acceptable as a single massing idea, but it remains closer to an abstract lifted block than a compact street building with an active ground edge. Sectionally, the form does not convincingly show a calm upper mass over a usable public void, so the program contract is only partially satisfied. It is not rejected for being too fragmented; rather, it fails the semantic ground relationship and public-space clarity expected of this program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller, tower-oriented typology; candidate is a low bar-like mass and lacks the vertical program expression.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single dominant prismatic volume can be legible when it is subtly tapered or stepped and still reads as one coherent mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower precedent; the candidate has no comparable vertical hierarchy or section-driven daylight logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clean monolithic mass can be made more articulate by a controlled profile shift or gentle twist while preserving continuity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference’s active corner/canopy is more program-specific than the candidate’s weakly opened base.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A neighborhood-scale building benefits from a legible ground response and a clear public edge rather than a sealed extrusion.

warnings: Primary road frontage/access edge appears to be answered on the wrong side or only indirectly; the visible mass does not clearly open to the verified access edge.
The interior void/cut is too small to read as usable public space in all four views.
Section program logic is weak: the mass reads more like a lifted box than a neighborhood building with an active ground threshold.
The candidate may survive as a generic massing object, but it does not hard-pass the neighborhood_living brief.
